item.title: Version 3.0.0
item.description:
Apple is retiring the Apple Ads API that ADSwift uses today on 26 January 2027. This update adds support for the new one. It’s off for now, so nothing changes until you choose to try it. You can switch back at any time, and your data and history stay as they are.

Added

  • A switch for the new Apple Ads API (beta). It’s in the Apple Ads status menu at the bottom of the window and in Settings → General. Turn it on to try the new API before it becomes the only one.
  • An “All ad positions” impression share column. With the new API, impression share shows exact percentages and your rank, both for the top of search results and across all ad positions.
  • See why a campaign is Limited or On Hold. With the new Apple Ads API, a small button next to the status shows Apple’s reasons — which countries are affected and what to do about each — for campaigns, ad groups and ads. Limited and On Hold now also have different colours.
  • Notes on campaigns, ad groups, keywords and negative keywords. Right-click and choose Add Note. A note icon next to the name shows which items have notes; hover it to read the latest, or click it to see them all. Notes also appear in each item’s detail panel.

Improved

  • Faster navigation. Going back is quicker, the campaign list keeps its place and revenue when you return, and opening a campaign no longer reloads every campaign. With the new API switched on, ad group and keyword numbers are ready the moment you open a campaign or ad group, instead of about a second later.

Fixed

  • Deleted keywords no longer come back after a refresh.
  • Ad groups on accounts that Apple moved to bid strategies work again. Creating an ad group or changing its bid was refused with “defaultBidAmount must be set to 0”, and these ad groups showed no bid.
  • Spend no longer shows $0 when it couldn’t be loaded. The menu bar now says the figure is unavailable instead.
  • Tables no longer draw their loading bars over the column headings.
  • Double-clicking a row no longer opens it twice, so Back takes you where you expect.
  • The Promote screen no longer draws its ad group list over everything else. With more than a few ad groups, the list spilled out over the destination options, the search field, the bids and the “Negate at source” toggle. It now stays in its own box and scrolls.
  • Duplicating a Maximize Conversions campaign no longer renames its automatic ad group. The copy’s automatic ad group was always called “Automatic Ad Group”, whatever the original’s was called. It now keeps the original’s name, and new Maximize Conversions campaigns name it “Automated”, as Apple Ads does.
